text: Account for the entire service life.

An engineered system moves through early planning and design, realization, service and support, and eventual withdrawal. Different management frameworks attach different names to those portions of work, and many engineering activities continue across several stages. Design decisions can shape later costs for training, spares, maintenance, improvements and end-of-life handling.

items: Illustration: Maintenance training needs to be developed before the system enters use and supported after it becomes operational.

text: Planning, acquisition, service, and retirement connect across the system life cycle.
Consider future operation and retirement while meaningful design alternatives remain.
A single fixed sequence does not replace overlapping technical processes.
